items.correct: Exploring HOW writers use language, form and structure to create meaning.
items.misconception: Just retelling the plot of the text.
items.why: Analysis interprets effects and ideas with evidence, not plot summary.

items.q: Is there only one correct interpretation of a poem?
items.correct: No — texts support multiple interpretations if backed by evidence.
items.misconception: Yes, every poem has a single correct meaning.
items.why: Strong responses offer a valid reading supported by quotations and analysis.

items.q: How should context be used when studying literature?
items.correct: Selectively, to illuminate the text's ideas and meaning.
items.misconception: By summarising the author's entire life story.
items.why: Relevant historical/social context deepens analysis when linked to the text, not bolted on.
